body: FLAG: in 2019 the Reddy family had pledged ~68-78% of its holding (reports: 'likely to hit 75%', Jul 2019); the family sold a 3.6% stake to cut it, taking its holding to ~30.8%. Our hard rule (pledge >25% or rising) disqualifies this. CONTEXT: (1) the pledge was at the family level, the listed company itself was not over-levered and its core hospitals were profitable (OPM 10-15%, CFO Rs 537-1,293 cr FY18-20); (2) purpose and lenders were disclosed and management publicly committed to a reduction path (to ~20-25% by Nov 2019); (3) the trend was falling, funded by actual stake sales rather than promises; (4) the group had no history of fund diversion. By Aug 2025 a 1.3% block sale (Rs 1,489 cr) cut the pledge from 13.1% to ~2% of promoter holding. ROCE recovered from 7% (FY18) to 17%. Stock: ~Rs 1,293 (2019) -> Rs 9,040 (Nov 2026), ~7x. HONEST CAVEAT: a 2020-style crash could have triggered invocations; it worked partly because the price rose. LESSON: pledge severity depends on purpose, % of holding, trend, lender type, company leverage and group history; a high but falling, disclosed, family-level pledge with a clean group is a sizing/monitoring issue, not proof of fraud.

data.context: family-level, disclosed purpose, falling via real stake sales, unlevered company, clean group
data.lesson: grade pledges; never treat as binary but size small
data.note: Prices/ratios: screener.in consolidated pages and chart API (split/bonus-adjusted closes), fetched 20-Nov-2026.

title: False alarm (with luck): Apollo Hospitals' 76% promoter pledge
